properties.name: Bill's Bay & Skeleton Beach Reef Walks
properties.location: Coral Bay, Ningaloo Reef Front
properties.comment: Walk the shallow northern limestone rocky flats at low tide. A legendary natural collector trap for bright orange cockles, patterned cone shells, and glossy cowries washed up from the fringing reef.

properties.name: Coalseam Riverbed Scramble
properties.location: Coalseam Conservation Park, Irwin River Bank
properties.comment: Walk right down onto the dry rocky riverbank. Flip over individual river stones to find 250-million-year-old brachiopod and marine bivalve imprints. Leave your finds on the bank for the next traveller!

properties.name: Eyre Highway Limestone Road-Cuts
properties.location: Nullarbor Plain, between Balladonia and Madura
properties.comment: Pull into major highway rest areas and inspect the rubble piles blasted from vertical limestone road-cut walls. Hundreds of sea shell casts, fossilised echinoids and bryozoans sit loose on the surface. Miner's Right required to collect.

properties.name: Fossil Picnic Area — Coalseam
properties.location: Coalseam Conservation Park, Irwin River Bank
properties.comment: Walk down onto the dry riverbed next to the picnic tables. Thousands of 250-million-year-old fossilised marine shells exposed across the surface of the stones.

properties.name: Flinders Bay Shell Grit Beds
properties.location: Augusta Region, near the harbour
properties.comment: Where the Indian and Southern Oceans collide. Rocky corners trap heavy shell grit layers after winter storms. Rock pools and weed lines yield large robust cold-water sea shells and tumbled granite pebbles.

properties.name: Gantheaume Beach Low Tide Pools
properties.location: Broome, Kimberley Coast
properties.comment: Massive tidal changes expose complex rock pools along the red pindan cliffs. Sandy pockets inside low-tide rock pools reveal tropical species like snakehead and ring-top cowries.

properties.name: Gantheaume Point Low Tide Reef Walk
properties.location: Broome, Kimberley Coastline
properties.comment: When the tide drops below 2.1 metres, climb onto the flat red sandstone shelf to search for 130-million-year-old dinosaur footprints. Excellent interpretive signs show you what shapes to look for.

properties.name: Gascoyne River Gravel Bars
properties.location: Gascoyne Junction area, dry riverbed sections
properties.comment: Walk the wide dry pebble and gravel curves of the riverbed. Flip over dark heavy siltstones to find detailed marine imprints including crinoid stems, spiriferid brachiopods and solitary corals. Miner's Right required.

properties.name: Gingin Chalk Exposure Areas
properties.location: Gingin Region
properties.comment: Famous zone for fossilised marine life and shark teeth. Requires contacting local managers or landowners before accessing the chalk faces. Miner's Right and landowner consent needed.

properties.name: Green Head Beachcombing Ledger
properties.location: Green Head, Mid-West Coast
properties.comment: One specific bay gets choked with trillions of tiny pristine pure-white shells. Collectors nickname them 'white rice' — almost identical in size and perfectly preserved.

properties.name: Hamelin Pool Stromatolites
properties.location: Shark Bay World Heritage Area
properties.comment: Active living fossils representing life on Earth from 3.5 billion years ago. Short walk to the old quarry and shoreline to see them in the shallow brine. One of the most significant fossil sites on Earth.

properties.name: Hopetoun Back Beach Shell Sifting
properties.location: Hopetoun, South Coast
properties.comment: Ocean currents dump a massive concentration of shells here. Sifting the shell grit reveals an exceptionally high percentage of deep pink, red, and chocolate-caramel whole shells.

properties.name: Minim Cove Fossil Bank
properties.location: Mosman Park, Perth Metro — Swan River
properties.comment: Secret hands-on spot right in Perth's suburbs. Run your hands along rocky limestone cliffs at the river's edge to spot thousands of ancient prehistoric bivalves, gastropods, and fossilised weevil cocoons.

properties.name: Norseman Public Fossicking Area
properties.location: Norseman Region, 10 km west of townsite
properties.type: Ancient Geologic Fossicking — Agate and Chert
properties.comment: The only official legal public fossicking area on a roadside layout in WA. Walk the open red dirt, kick over stones, search the gravel — and you are allowed to keep what you find here!

properties.name: Point Peron Rock & Shell Search
properties.location: Rockingham Region
properties.comment: Walk rugged honeycombed limestone headlands and sandy coves. Known hotspot for beach-polished sea glass, iridescent shells, and fossilised plant root tracks in the ancient limestone.

properties.name: Shell Beach Conservation Park
properties.location: Shark Bay World Heritage Area
properties.comment: One of only two beaches in the world made 100% from shells. Trillions of tiny white Hamelin Cockle shells go up to 10 metres deep. Walk and read the educational signs about why they thrive here.

properties.name: Turquoise Bay Drift Shoreline
properties.location: Cape Range National Park, Exmouth
properties.comment: Heavy drift current pushes unique deep-sea treasures onto the tide lines. Search for olive shells, heavy-spined murex, and moon snails. Ningaloo is a marine park — look, photograph, and leave them for the ecosystem.

properties.name: Windjana Gorge Ancient Coral Reef
properties.location: Kimberley Region, Napier Range
properties.comment: The towering canyon walls are a 350-million-year-old barrier reef. Look along the vertical rock face near the entry gate for fossilised extinct corals and sponges frozen in the dark grey stone.

properties.name: Eighty Mile Beach
properties.location: Between Port Hedland and Broome
properties.comment: Widely regarded as one of the best shell collecting beaches in the world. Massive 9-metre tides clear the sand flats twice daily, leaving thousands of pristine giant shells. Famous for intact Mother-of-Pearl, sand dollars, and massive bailer shells.

properties.name: Molecap Quarry — Gingin Chalk
properties.location: Off Cockram Road, 1 km from Gingin town centre
properties.type: Cretaceous Shark Teeth, Mosasaur and Plesiosaur Bones
properties.access: 2WD — private wheat farm, historically tolerated via low sheep gate off Cockram Road. Landowner permission recommended.
properties.comment: One of WA's most significant fossil sites. The Molecap Greensand yields shark teeth, mosasaur arm bones, plesiosaur vertebrae up to 120mm, ichthyosaur vertebrae, and the only dinosaur bone found in WA (theropod toe bone, 1992). Chalk layer above contains ammonites, giant clam Inoceramus, crinoids and brachiopods. 80-85 million years old. Miner's Right required.

properties.name: Contos Beach Garnets
properties.location: Contos Beach, south of Margaret River
properties.comment: Garnets found in the rocky limestone platforms and sand at low tide. Personal find — collected quite a few here. Best searched at low tide around the rocky outcrops.

properties.name: Cancanning Meteorite Fall
properties.location: 12 km north-north-east of Gundaring, near Cancanning Hall, Wheatbelt
properties.comment: On April 6 1930 a fireball with loud rumbling and explosion was witnessed across the Pingelly-Cuballing district. Not found until May 1937 when F. Quinn discovered a piece on Block 14355 near Cancanning Hall. The 43x42x23cm specimen is now at the WA Museum. A rock fell from space and sat in a paddock for seven years.

properties.name: Preston River Gold — Beelerup
properties.location: Preston River at Beelerup Road, near Donnybrook
properties.comment: Very small fern vein gold reported in the Donnybrook area. Creek beds where water slows are classic gold trapping locations. The Darling Range greenstone belt geology is right for it. Miner's Right required.

properties.name: Volutoconus hargreavesi — NW Cape Deep Water
properties.location: North West Cape, Exmouth Region
properties.comment: One of WA's rarest volutes. Lives at 100–160m depth and almost never found alive — look for dead-washed specimens after storms on NW Cape beaches. Stunning elongated shape with fine brown banding on cream. WA endemic. WAM specimens collected 2001. Serious collector's shell.

properties.name: Amoria diamantina — NW Cape Offshore
properties.location: West of North West Cape, Exmouth Region
properties.comment: Named after the Diamantina Trench. WA endemic and genuinely rare — lives at 68m depth. Gorgeous flame-pattern volute in orange and cream. WAM specimens dredged 1964–1972. Almost never turns up on beaches; a storm-washed find would be exceptional.

properties.name: Amoria rinkensi — NW Shelf Deep Slope
properties.location: North West Shelf Slope, off Exmouth
properties.access: Beach access 2WD — exceptionally rare dead-washed find
properties.comment: Deep-water rarity found at 220m on the NW Shelf slope. Barely ever surfaces. WAM specimen collected 2002. If you find one on a beach it has travelled a very long way. Small, smooth, with delicate patterning.

properties.name: Cymbiola nivosa — Vlamingh Head Beaches
properties.location: North West Cape, Vlamingh Head to Learmonth
properties.comment: The Snowy Volute — WA's most iconic large volute. Creamy white with bold dark brown spots. Multiple WAM records from Vlamingh Head, Point Cloates, and Learmonth beaches 1964–1984. A big, beautiful shell worth stopping for. Look along high-tide wrack lines after storms.

properties.name: Nannamoria capricornea — Point Cloates Offshore
properties.location: West of Point Cloates, Ningaloo
properties.comment: Small, deep-water WA endemic volute named for the Capricorn region. Found at 71m depth. Rare and seldom seen. WAM specimens dredged 1964–1972 west of Point Cloates. A quiet little rarity.

properties.name: Amoria praetexta — Bundegi Reef
properties.location: Exmouth Gulf, Bundegi Reef
properties.comment: A lovely smaller volute found at Bundegi Reef in 1969. Less rare than its Volutidae cousins but a genuine find. Cream with fine brown axial lines. Look along the reef rubble and wrack line at low tide.

properties.name: Gloripallium pallium — Muiron Islands
properties.location: South Muiron Island, Exmouth Gulf
properties.access: Boat access from Tantabiddi or Exmouth
properties.comment: The Royal Cloak Scallop. Deep crimson and white fan shell — one of the most striking scallops in WA waters. WAM specimens from South Muiron Island reefs. Found on rubble and coral at depth; dead-washed valves occasionally on beaches after rough weather.

properties.name: Mimachlamys gloriosa — North West Cape Reef
properties.location: North West Cape, reef areas
properties.access: 2WD to cape — snorkel or low-tide reef walk
properties.comment: The Glorious Scallop. The name is not an exaggeration — richly ribbed and coloured in reds, purples, and whites. WAM specimen from NW Cape. One of WA's most beautiful bivalves. Look on reef rubble or in shallow rocky areas.

properties.name: Excellichlamys spectabilis — South Muiron Island
properties.location: Exmouth Gulf, South Muiron Island
properties.comment: The Spectacular Scallop — and yes, it earns that name. Large, glossy, strongly ribbed with vivid colour variation from orange to purple. WAM specimen from South Muiron Island. A serious find for any shell collector.

properties.name: Cymbiola irvinae — Irwin's Volute Range
properties.location: SW WA Coast — Kalbarri to Augusta
properties.comment: Irwin's Volute — a WA endemic and genuinely rare find. GBIF records span Kalbarri south through Cervantes, Rottnest, Fremantle and the south coast to Augusta. One specimen found at 54m depth off Fremantle; most records are beach-washed. Cream with fine brown flame markings, medium-large shell. Named for Bruce Wilson's colleague. If you find one on a SW WA beach you've done well. Pin placed at Kalbarri — the northernmost confirmed record.

properties.name: Melo miltonis — Milton's Volute Beaches
properties.location: SW WA Coast — Lancelin to Augusta
properties.comment: Milton's Volute — WA's great southern giant. One of the largest gastropods in WA waters, creamy orange with bold brown zigzag markings. Recent iNaturalist records (2025–2026) place it along the entire SW coast from Lancelin through Perth beaches, Mandurah, Busselton and down to Augusta and Esperance. Look along high-tide wrack lines after winter storms — these wash up whole. Bigger and heavier than you expect. Pin placed near Quinns Rocks where multiple 2026 records cluster.

properties.name: Zoila friendii — Carnac Island & Cockburn Sound
properties.location: Woodman Point, Cockburn Sound, south of Fremantle
properties.access: 2WD to Woodman Point — boat to Carnac Island
properties.comment: Friend's Cowrie — WA's most celebrated cowrie and a serious collector's shell. Large, heavy, deep chocolate brown above with a pure white base and fine teeth. WA endemic. Cockburn Sound and Carnac Island are the most consistently recorded locations going back to 1962. Found at 1–15m depth on reef and rubble. Dead-washed specimens occasionally on nearby beaches after storms. WAM records span 1962–2008.

properties.name: Zoila friendii — Geographe Bay
properties.location: Geographe Bay, between Busselton and Dunsborough
properties.comment: Friend's Cowrie hotspot — more records from Geographe Bay than almost anywhere else in WA. WAM specimens collected 1960–1989 along this stretch. Found at 6m depth on reef. Look along the reef edges between Dunsborough and Busselton. Recent iNaturalist sightings confirm it's still here. One of the best spots on the SW coast to find this species.

properties.name: Zoila friendii — Albany Reefs
properties.location: Albany, Great Southern Coast
properties.access: 2WD — boat or dive access to reefs
properties.comment: Friend's Cowrie at the southern end of its range. Multiple WAM records from Albany 1983–1999 at 13–40m depth — these are deeper water finds, mostly dredged or diver-collected. Dead-washed valves occasionally on beaches after heavy Southern Ocean swells. Worth checking reef rubble and kelp beds around King George Sound.

properties.name: Zoila friendii — Esperance Reefs
properties.location: Esperance, South Coast
properties.comment: Friend's Cowrie at the eastern edge of its WA range. WAM records from Esperance 1995–2001 at 6.5–37.5m depth. The Recherche Archipelago reefs offshore from Esperance are rich hunting ground. A find here would be at the limit of the species' known distribution — worth noting if you find one.

properties.name: Campanile symbolicum — Rottnest Island
properties.location: Rottnest Island & Garden Island, off Fremantle
properties.access: Ferry to Rottnest — snorkel or low tide reef walk
properties.comment: The Giant Campanile — a living fossil and WA's most iconic shell. This species was thought extinct for 40 million years until found alive off WA in the 1890s. A tall, heavy, ribbed gastropod up to 30cm. Rottnest Island is one of the most consistently recorded locations — Armstrong Bay, The Grottos, Thomson Bay, Parker Point. Found at 4–10m depth on seagrass beds. Dead-washed shells occasionally on beaches. Records span 1912 to 2026 — it's still here.

properties.name: Campanile symbolicum — Cape Naturaliste to Yallingup
properties.location: Bunker Bay, Cape Naturaliste, Yallingup, Dunsborough
properties.comment: One of the densest clusters of Campanile records on the WA coast. WAM specimens from Bunker Bay, Cape Naturaliste, Yallingup and Dunsborough going back to 1954. Found in seagrass at 6–15m depth. Dead shells wash onto beaches along this stretch regularly. This is Margaret River wine country with a living fossil in the water — not a bad combination.

properties.name: Campanile symbolicum — Albany Coast
properties.location: Albany, King George Sound and surrounds
properties.comment: Albany is a Campanile hotspot — multiple WAM records from 1910 onwards and iNaturalist sightings right through to 2026. Found at 8.5m depth in King George Sound. Dead shells wash up on local beaches after Southern Ocean swells. The sheer span of records here — over 100 years — says something about how consistently this species occupies this stretch of coast.

properties.name: Campanile symbolicum — Jurien Bay to Green Head
properties.location: Mid-West Coast, Jurien Bay region
properties.comment: Northern extent of Campanile's SW WA range. Records from Green Head, Jurien Bay and Escape Island going back to 1958 with recent sightings to 2025. Beach-washed shells found along this limestone coast. Worth checking the wrack line on beaches between Green Head and Jurien after winter swells.

properties.name: Altivasum flindersi — Cape Leeuwin Deep Water
properties.location: Cape Leeuwin to Geographe Bay, SW Corner WA
properties.comment: Flinders' Vase — one of WA's most extraordinary deep water shells. A tall, elegant vase-shaped volute with fine sculpting, found at depth off the SW corner of WA. Records from Cape Leeuwin, Geographe Bay, Mandurah and Esperance — all dead-washed or dredged. Lives too deep to find alive. If one washes up on a beach near Cape Leeuwin or Augusta after a big Southern Ocean swell, you have found something genuinely rare. Related species Altivasum hedleyi also recorded in this area.

properties.name: Argonauta argo — Paper Nautilus Beaches
properties.location: SW WA Coast — Augusta to Albany, also Eighty Mile Beach
properties.comment: The Paper Nautilus — not a true nautilus but an octopus whose female secretes a breathtakingly fragile white paper-thin egg case to carry her young. One of the most beautiful accidental finds on any beach. WA records run from Eighty Mile Beach in the north all the way to Albany — but the SW corner around Augusta, Cape Leeuwin and Denmark sees the most consistent strandings after Southern Ocean swells. Translucent white, ribbed, impossibly delicate. Walk slowly and look carefully — they shatter easily. Pin placed near Augusta where multiple records cluster.
